nodes.description: Biallelic COL1A2 null variants destabilize the transcript. Splice-site variants lead to use of cryptic splice donor sites, creating a downstream premature termination codon and extremely unstable mRNA; homozygous nonsense codons act directly. Either route engages the nonsense-mediated RNA decay pathway, so essentially no COL1A2 message survives to be translated. The order in which neighboring introns are removed is an important determinant of whether a given splice-site variant produces exon skipping or this decay-activating outcome.
nodes.id: COL1A2 Null Allele and Nonsense-Mediated mRNA Decay

nodes.description: Type I collagen is normally a heterotrimer of two proα1(I) chains and one proα2(I) chain. With no proα2(I) available, the molecule is assembled instead as an α1(I) homotrimer. This altered composition is detectable by SDS-PAGE analysis of collagens extracted from cultured skin fibroblasts, which remains a practical way to identify affected individuals.

evidence.snippet: Homozygous or compound heterozygous COL1A2 mutations resulting in complete deficiency of the proalpha2(I) collagen chains are extremely rare and have been reported in only a few patients, albeit with variable phenotypic outcome.

nodes.description: Generalized or peripheral joint hypermobility with skin hyperextensibility, soft skin, atrophic scarring, and easy bruising. Bone fragility is characteristically absent — the feature that separates cvEDS from the recessive osteogenesis imperfecta also caused by biallelic COL1A2 variants, and from dominant osteogenesis imperfecta with severe valve disease. In childhood this arm can resemble mild hypermobile EDS, which is why the diagnosis is often not suspected until valve disease appears.

evidence.snippet: The absence of bone fragility in our patients indicates that cardiac valvular EDS is also separated from patients with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta and variants in COL1A2, as well as from individuals with autosomal dominant osteogenesis imperfecta and severe cardiac valvular disease.

nodes.description: Valve leaflet extracellular matrix, which depends on normal type I collagen, degenerates progressively. The mitral valve is affected first, with the aortic valve involved later, producing moderate-to-severe valvular insufficiency. Because valve disease can emerge well after the soft-tissue features, it may not be apparent in childhood.
